gbm_population_evidence.quote: Recurrent Glioblastoma; Recurrent Astrocytoma; Recurrent Oligodendroglioma; Recurrent Glioma
Patients must have histologically proven high-grade gliomas - GBM, Astrocytoma, or Oligodendroglioma (glioma WHO Grade III or IV) that is now recurrent by MRI or surgical pathology.

candidate_evidence.quote: The starting dose will be 300 mg niraparib (or modified according patient weight and platelet count), taken orally once a day for each cycle of 28 days.
Percentage of patients who respond to niraparib monitored by disease control rate (stable disease and better) using RANO from start of treatment for up to 12 months.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Phase II Trial of Niraparib in Patients With Recurrent Glioma

role_evidence.quote: Patients will be treated with individualized starting dose of Niraparib.

agents.drug_class_hint: PARP inhibitor, approved for ovarian cancer

biomarkers.biomarker_other: homologous recombination deficiency / genomic instability (Myriad myChoice assay)

source_quote.quote: Patient has archival tumor tissue available; or a fresh biopsy of recurrent or persistent tumor must be obtained for molecular assay by myChoice test (Myriad Genetics) prior to study treatment initiation.

flag.reason: Tissue for the myChoice HRD assay is required before treatment, but no assay result is required for entry; coded exploratory_correlative, though could be read as an eligibility biomarker matched to niraparib (primary outcome).

coder_notes: Mixed high-grade glioma (grade III/IV) trial with GBM named in conditions and inclusion; no IDH requirement, WHO grade III/IV terminology, so historical. The myChoice test (HRD status) is mechanistically linked to PARP inhibition but the record does not state that a positive result is required. Prior PARP inhibitor exclusion is prior-therapy, not a biomarker. No PK or PD planned.
